description: Logos, icons, banners, social images, and CIP deliverables. These gates run against the exported files, not the source that produced them.

gates.title: Logo Ships With A Transparent Background
gates.rule: The delivered logo has an alpha channel and its corners are actually transparent. A mark generated on white is a mark that shows a white box on every surface that is not white. Generation on white is a prompt technique, not a deliverable - the background comes off before hand-off.
gates.fix: Run scripts/logo/transparent.py on the export, then re-verify. Deliver the transparent file; keep the white-background render only as a preview.

gates.title: Every SVG Ships With A Transparent Background
gates.rule: AST-01 holds the raster exports; this holds the vector ones, and it holds all of them - marks, icons, favicons, plates, artwork out of a generator. A graphic carries its drawing and nothing behind it, so it reads the same on a dark band, a light card, and a page that changes theme under it. The ground, where one is wanted, is a class on whatever renders the file. The exceptions are the backings that hold something up rather than sit behind it - a QR code's quiet zone, a scrim with a spotlight masked out of it, a noise texture - and each of those is a shape the measure already passes rather than a licence to paint a canvas.
gates.fix: Run ~/.claude/tools/svg-guard.py fix on the export directory, then put any ground the design wants on the element that renders the file.

gates.title: Logo Ships In Vector Where It Can
gates.rule: An SVG accompanies the raster wherever the mark is vectorisable. A logo that only exists as a PNG cannot go on a vehicle or a sign.

gates.title: Logo Legible At Minimum Size
gates.rule: Rendered at 16px, 32px, and its stated minimum, the mark still reads. Detail that disappears at favicon size is detail the mark does not need.

gates.title: Light And Dark Variants Delivered
gates.rule: A variant that reads on a light surface and one that reads on a dark surface. One file is half a delivery.

gates.title: Icons Are SVG With A Consistent Grid
gates.rule: One viewBox, one stroke width, one visual weight across the set. Icons sit on the same optical grid so they do not jitter in a row.

gates.title: Icons Inherit Colour
gates.rule: Icons use currentColor rather than a baked fill, so they follow the three themes rather than fighting them.
gates.fix: Replace hardcoded fill and stroke values with currentColor.

gates.title: Exported At The Exact Platform Size
gates.rule: The file's pixel dimensions match the platform specification exactly - not close, exactly. A cover image one pixel off gets recompressed and softened.

gates.title: Critical Content Inside The Safe Zone
gates.rule: Everything that must be read sits in the central 70-80%. Platform chrome, avatars, and crops eat the edges.

gates.title: One CTA, Placed And Sized
gates.rule: A single call to action, bottom-right, at least 44px tall.

gates.title: Two Fonts, Body 16px+, Headline 32px+
gates.rule: At most two faces on a banner; body no smaller than 16px; headline no smaller than 32px.

gates.title: Ad Text Under 20% Of The Image
gates.rule: Meta penalises reach past roughly 20% text coverage. Measured, not estimated.

gates.title: Print Output Is 300 DPI, CMYK, With Bleed
gates.rule: 300 DPI, CMYK colour, 3-5mm bleed on every edge that runs off the page.

gates.title: Every Requested Size Was Produced
gates.rule: Each platform and size the brief named exists as a file. A set delivered short is a set the user has to chase.

gates.title: Exports Are Named And Optimised
gates.rule: Consistent, sortable filenames that say platform and size; file sizes optimised for the medium; email assets under 1MB.

gates.title: Every Export Was Looked At
gates.rule: Each exported file was opened at full size and inspected - not assumed correct because the HTML looked right. Text baked into an image cannot be fixed later.

gates.title: CIP Deliverables Cover The Named Set
gates.rule: Each deliverable the brief asked for exists, with the logo placed to its usage rules on every one.
